title: PowerPoint on Mac: reference SharePoint and OneDrive files when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: the briefing says Microsoft has not described how the capability arrives, but the cited release notes explain that Copilot features roll out gradually within tenants. The roadmap facts, licensing-assignment controls and Restricted Content Discovery controls are supported; feature-specific entitlement and handling of explicitly named files remain undocumented.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 555897 describes referencing SharePoint library and OneDrive folder files when creating presentations with Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot can recognize a SharePoint or OneDrive file mentioned by file or document name in a PowerPoint prompt.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint can now recognize references to files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive when you mention them in your prompt, such as by file or document name.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope
claims.claim: Copilot can use the referenced file as context when creating the presentation.
claims.quote: You can naturally reference a relevant file in your prompt, and Copilot can use that file as context when creating your presentation.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot presents only data each individual can access using existing Microsoft 365 data-access controls.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits discovery of selected SharePoint sites in organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot responses.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses
claims.fix: Add: 'Microsoft pages differ on recently interacted content: the Restricted Content Discovery page includes recently interacted files in its scope, while https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/copilot-search-manage#manage-access-to-files-and-sites says sites are excluded unless the user owns or has recently interacted with their content.' Cite that second page.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery supports SharePoint sites, not OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites. It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes discoverability, not existing permissions.
claims.quote: No. Restricted Content Discovery affects discoverability, not access permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access it.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not specifically describe whether Restricted Content Discovery stops a file explicitly named in a PowerPoint prompt.
claims.quote: Searched: Restricted Content Discovery PowerPoint file name prompt implicit references RestrictContentOrgWideSearch. Read restricted-content-discovery, release-note entry and Copilot Search search excerpt; none explicitly addresses named-file PowerPoint prompts.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery updates are not immediately effective because they must propagate.
claims.quote: Because the setting must propagate across indexing systems, updates can take time to become fully effective.

claims.claim: For sites with more than 500,000 items, Restricted Content Discovery updates could take more than a week to fully process.
claims.quote: For sites with more than 500,000 items, an update to Restricted Content Discovery could take more than a week to fully process and reflect in search and Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: The SharePoint admin center path is Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site. Use PowerShell: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: License assignment is under Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PowerShell can assign a selected SKU with Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @().
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: License Administrator or User Administrator is the minimum role for assigning licenses on the cited admin page.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.
